transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Maya (Aperture CTO), Liam (Lead Eng), Priya (Security)

Summary: quick integration discovery focusing on SDK support, LangChain/LlamaIndex workflows, gateway/proxy architecture for private deployments, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) with security controls and SSO/KMS requirements.

Topics: SDK languages, LangChain + LlamaIndex connectors, proxy/gateway patterns, rate limiting and per-route quotas, observability/tracing, token-level cost visibility, SOC2/KMS, data residency

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Samira, AE on the account, with Daniel from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Maya (Aperture): Hey thanks, doing good. We wanna dive into integration details — especially LangChain + LlamaIndex since we're building a commerce search assistant.
[00:12] Daniel (Redwood SE): Great. Quick agenda — SDK support (python/node/go), LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, options for gateway or proxy when using Redwood Private, rate limits and per-route quotas, and observability hooks (traces, token-level cost). Sound OK?
[00:22] Liam (Lead Eng): Yep. We'll also flag security requirements — SSO, KMS, retention.
[00:26] Priya (Security): And audit logs, obviously.
[00:28] Samira: Cool. To start — what does your stack look like today?
[00:32] Maya: We run microservices on k8s in AWS, have an internal gateway, and a vector DB (Milvus) for embeddings. Front end calls a search service which then does embedding lookups. We're evaluating Redwood for generation + embeddings. Key must-haves: VPC/private deployment or dedicated capacity, SSO (SAML), audit logs, and KMS integration for encryption.
[00:48] Daniel: That aligns with a lot we see. On SDKs — Redwood has official SDKs for Python and Node, plus a simple HTTP REST API. We also have community-supported Go and Java SDKs. For LangChain and LlamaIndex, we provide direct connectors and examples. The LangChain examples show the chain/agent flow, and we have LlamaIndex mappings for document loaders and embedding functions.
[01:10] Liam: Are those connectors first-class or community forks?
[01:12] Daniel: They are maintained by Redwood's SDK team — first-party examples and a small client helper. We bundle code snippets in the quickstart. There are occasional community extensions but the main examples are official.
[01:22] Maya: For embeddings, what about vector DB integrations? We saw examples for Pinecone and Milvus?
[01:27] Daniel: Yes. We have sample code for Pinecone, Milvus, and FAISS, and an end-to-end example showing embeddings ingestion + similarity search + generation fallback.
[01:36] Priya: On Private deployment — how does the gateway/proxy work? We need to keep keys inside our VPC and not expose traffic externally.
[01:42] Samira: Good question. Daniel, wanna take the Private flow?
[01:44] Daniel: Sure. For Redwood Private we can either run a customer-hosted gateway that forwards requests to a customer-controlled control plane, or we can place our runtime inside your VPC. Typical pattern is a lightweight proxy that handles auth, rate limiting, and logging — it can rotate API keys and do signing. That proxy sits in your network and calls Redwood's runtime endpoints over private peering or an encrypted tunnel.
[02:05] Maya: So keys never leave our environment?
[02:07] Daniel: Correct if you run the gateway/proxy. Alternatively, with Dedicated you can have reserved capacity and stricter IP allowlists, but keys flow through Redwood-managed endpoints. With Private VPC/on-prem you keep keys in your KMS and control ingress.
[02:19] Liam: What about latency — if we host gateway and runtime in AWS region, what numbers should we expect?
[02:24] Daniel: For standard open models, p50 token latency is usually in the low tens of ms per token on A100-class instances; end-to-end across a gateway in the same region we're talking sub-200ms for short completions. Dedicated pools give predictable throughput; Private inside your VPC removes public network hops. We'll share our performance profiles.
[02:41] Maya: Good. Rate limits — we need per-user and per-route quotas, also burst control. Can Redwood do that at the gateway level or do we need additional infra?
[02:50] Samira: We have rate limiting at both Redwood's API and you can enforce it in the gateway. Redwood's quotas support per-api-key quotas and per-route limits. For Private, the gateway can enforce user-level rules and integrate with your auth.
[03:03] Priya: Do you provide middleware or policies for that?
[03:06] Daniel: We provide example config for Envoy and NGINX as proxy templates, and a small Redwood policy library that plugs into your gateway. It emits metrics compatible with Prometheus. The proxy also supports token bucket and leaky-bucket algorithms.
[03:19] Liam: Observability — we need traces tied to our request IDs, token-level cost metrics, and per-model breakdowns.
[03:26] Daniel: Redwood Console has per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level costs, and tracing hooks. For Private, we can forward traces to your OTLP collector, and the gateway can add X-Request-ID headers. You can also ingest logs into your ELK/Datadog via forwarders.
[03:39] Maya: Do you emit detailed prompt/response payloads in logs? We have data residency concerns.
[03:44] Daniel: By default we log metadata — latencies, model, token counts. Payload logging is opt-in and can be disabled; for Private we can configure no payload retention and only store hashes for audit. KMS integration for key rotation is supported.
[03:56] Priya: SOC2/ISO stuff — are you SOC2 type II?
[03:59] Samira: Yes, we are SOC2 Type II. We'll share the report under an NDA. Also have ISO controls for enterprise customers.
[04:07] Liam: Any pre-built rate-limiting metrics in console? Need alerts when token spend exceeds a threshold.
[04:12] Daniel: Console supports alerting and budget thresholds per project. You can attach webhooks on budget events; we can also push anomalies to your pager system.
[04:20] Maya: For the LangChain flow — we want to run a pipeline where a user query first hits our search + rerank, then embeddings, then a call to Redwood generate. Can we do caching of KV cache or prefix caching?
[04:32] Daniel: Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching to reduce cost and speed up common paths. For chains that reuse context, you'll see big savings. We also recommend caching embeddings at the vector DB side to avoid re-embedding.
[04:43] Liam: Are there limits on KV cache size or eviction policies?
[04:46] Daniel: Configurable per-deployment — you can choose LRU or TTL-based eviction. For Dedicated pools we allocate local cache. For Private, you control sizing.
[04:54] Priya: About SDK auth and rotation — we use short-lived credentials from our IdP. Can we do token exchange?
[04:59] Daniel: Yes, we support token exchange and short-lived API tokens via our session API. For SAML/SSO we integrate with your IdP and support SCIM for provisioning.
[05:09] Maya: What about quota billing — do you bill per-token for hosted, and for Dedicated is it committed capacity?
[05:14] Samira: Hosted is usage-based (per-token + embeddings). Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit and overage rules. Private is enterprise license + optional commit for runtime resources. We'll include pricing examples in the follow-up.
[05:25] Liam: One more — do you have a reference PoC repo for LangChain and LlamaIndex with Milvus?
[05:30] Daniel: Yes, I'll share a GitHub repo. It includes a small demo using LangChain agent, embedding pipeline to Milvus, and a sample proxy config for Envoy.
[05:36] Maya: Great. Any limitations on model variants — do you do multi-model routing? For example route cheaper models for drafts and higher-quality for final generation?
[05:44] Daniel: Yes, routing policies are built-in. You can implement cost-based routing or latency-based. We also support automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants when capacity tightens.
[05:53] Priya: Encryption at rest and key management — we need HSM/KMS support and rotation logs.
[05:58] Daniel: We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and have HSM path for on-prem. We surface key rotation events in audit logs.
[06:06] Maya: Any gotchas when using LlamaIndex connectors? We use custom document loaders.
[06:11] Daniel: You can plug custom loaders — LlamaIndex examples show how to wrap your loader, and our embedding function is standard. There may be occasional tokenizer differences between embedding models; we'll note recommended tokenizers.
[06:22] Samira: Ok, let's talk about a pilot — would you prefer Hosted trial or Dedicated eval?
[06:27] Maya: We want to prove integration quickly with Hosted, then move to Dedicated or Private depending on security checks.
[06:33] Samira: Makes sense. We'll provision a trial API key with limited quota, send the LangChain/LlamaIndex PoC, and share SOC2/security docs.
[06:41] Liam: Timeline wise — we want a proof-of-concept in 2 weeks if possible.
[06:44] Daniel: That's reasonable for a basic LangChain demo. For Dedicated/Private evals we'd need infra planning — maybe 4-6 weeks.
[06:52] Maya: For next steps please include concrete examples for proxy config and how to wire OTLP.
[06:57] Samira: Will do.
[07:00] -- short crosstalk as people confirm availability --
[07:18] Daniel: I'll also include sample rate limit configs and an example of per-route quotas and webhook alerts for overspend.
[07:25] Priya: Please include the data retention defaults and how to disable payload logging.
[07:30] Samira: Noted.
[07:32] Maya: Awesome. Anything else from your side?
[07:35] Liam: Just curious — any existing customers with Milvus we can reference?
[07:39] Samira: We have a couple of retail customers using Milvus; we'll include anonymized notes and a short case study.
[07:46] Daniel: One more technical note — when you run the gateway we support mTLS between gateway and runtime for mutual auth.
[07:53] Maya: Good.
[07:55] Samira: Ok let's recap next steps.
[07:58] -- Recap and close --
[08:00] Samira: Action items, we'll: send integration guide + pricing (Samira), share PoC repo and code snippets (Daniel), provision trial API key (Samira), and Aperture to share traffic profile and vector DB details (Maya). We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the technical deep dive.
[08:20] Maya: Thanks everyone, meeting useful.
[08:24] Samira: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes on transcription: some words may be slightly off—e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache" occurred in a couple spots in auto transcript; speaker labels were manually cleaned but still reflect informal naming. There are occasional filler words and crosstalk.
